hook: SCP-1535 is a glass mason jar from 1946 that, once sealed, turns whatever small creature is inside into a reasoning, Spanish-speaking Catholic who knows Morse code. The article is short, and nearly all of its weight sits in one interview with a firefly. Pay attention to who the creature believes it is addressing, and to how casually the researcher answers.
whyItMatters: It shows how far a single test log can carry an article whose anomaly is simple on paper. The religious framing turns a routine interview into something uneasy, and the gap between the speaker's reverence and the researcher's offhand replies makes the scene darkly funny and cruel at the same time. The researcher's closing note then turns one conversation into a pattern.
thingsToNotice:
The firefly greets the researcher as its Father, gives its name, says it died of a sinful disease, and asks to be accepted for its faithfulness; Breen plays along with short answers and an easy forgiveness, then calls the interview finished. As the jar is about to be taken away, the light flashes faster and the creature pleads that it destroyed evil men in God's service, batters itself against the glass, and asks whether this is Hell. Breen's answer is a shrugging 'not really'.

The procedures make the situation bleaker in hindsight: the lid will not come off while an occupant lives, and each one suffocates within an hour or two, so this exchange is always the last thing it experiences. The final note adds that every occupant so far has claimed to be someone who died in Castile between 1500 and 1600.
